RagShortTexts: Riga commanded the Daugava estuary as the ecclesiastical and crusading spearhead of Livonia.

Variants.Content: Riga stood near the mouth of the Daugava and served as the crusading and commercial hub of Livonia. The city was shared between the Prince-Archbishop of Riga and the Livonian Order, a division of power that often produced friction between the two. Its fortified harbour funnelled furs and wax from Russian lands to the Hanseatic ports of the west, so a large part of the city's income came from long-distance trade. Merchants and clergy alike depended on the harbour and had reason to keep the river route safe. The crusading wars in the Baltic gave Riga its military role, while its commerce gave it wealth, and the balance between the two shaped nearly every decision its rulers made.
Stone battlements sheltered German burghers from indigenous revolts, anchoring Christian feudal colonisation along the eastern Baltic.
